segments.text: In this code walkthrough we build a token bucket rate limiter.
A rate limiter caps how many requests a client can make per second.
The token bucket holds tokens that refill at a fixed rate.
Each incoming request must remove one token to proceed.
If the bucket is empty the request is rejected with status code 429.
We store the token count and the last refill timestamp per client.
On each request we compute how many tokens to add since the last refill.
The refill amount is elapsed time multiplied by the refill rate.
We cap the token count at the bucket capacity to prevent bursts.
For distributed systems we store the state in Redis instead of memory.
Redis lets multiple servers share one consistent limit per client.
We use a Lua script so the check and update happen atomically.
Finally we return the remaining tokens in a response header.
That completes our token bucket rate limiter implementation.
